summary: Small, correctly-scoped fix in DelegatingParser.parse_delta: when a reasoning parser confirms end-of-reasoning without surfacing the trailing content as streamed content (engine-confirmed reasoning end paired with a text-based tool parser), the content after the marker is recovered by decoding the extracted content token ids so the text-based tool parser can see it. Comes with a genuine regression test that fails without the change, and I confirmed no regressions across the combined engine/streaming suites.
actions_taken: Read the diff and surrounding code in vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py: the change is entirely inside the `if should_transition:` reasoning->tool transition, in the non-fully-engine-based `else` branch (lines ~853-864). Traced the two engine flags: `reasoning_parser.engine_based_streaming` (transition detection) vs `self._engine_based` (True only when BOTH reasoning and tool are engine-based). The new code runs only when reasoning end is confirmed but delta_message.content is empty AND extract_content_ids returned tokens.

Traced blast radius. For text-based reasoning parsers (BaseThinkingReasoningParser), extract_reasoning_streaming already populates delta_message.content when there is trailing content, and returns empty content exactly when extract_content_ids returns [] (end token at end of delta / single-special-token skip). So `not current_text and current_token_ids` is False in those cases and the new lines are a no-op — no double-emit / no regression for the common text-reasoning path. The new lines only take effect for engine-confirmed reasoning end + text-based tool parser (the case the fix targets).

Confirmed the new test is genuine coverage (fails without the change): without the recovery, delta 2 ('</think><') yields current_text='' so the leading '<' is dropped from the text stream while its token id is carried in previous_token_ids; on delta 3 the text-based Hermes parser then sees 'tool_call>...' without the leading '<', fails to match <tool_call>, and leaks the whole call into content. The test asserts the tool call is parsed and 'tool_call' not in content.

Ran: PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=$(mktemp -d) .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/test_streaming.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -> 14 passed, 2 failed. The new test test_parse_delta_engine_reasoning_tool_batched_boundary passes (also verified in isolation: 1 passed). The 2 failures are test_parse_delta_required_tool_choice_kimi_k2_ids[_after_history], which use reasoning=False (no reasoning parser); _in_reasoning_phase() is therefore always False, so the changed branch is never executed — pre-existing failures unrelated to this diff.
Ran combined engine reasoning+tool suites: tests/parser/engine/test_delegating_replay.py, test_qwen3.py, test_minimax_m2.py, test_qwen3_reasoning.py -> 893 passed. No regressions.

Ran full tests/parser/engine/, tests/parser/test_parse.py, tests/parser/test_harmony.py, tests/tool_parsers/test_hermes_tool_parser.py -> 3722 passed, 1 skipped, 39 failed. All 39 failures are in test_harmony.py and are environmental: openai_harmony.HarmonyError 'failed to download or load vocab file' (network/vocab download blocked). The gpt-oss harmony path is a separate parser and does not exercise the changed code; these are not caused by the diff.

Checked which real parsers set engine_based_streaming=True (only the ParserEngine adapters in vllm/parser/engine/adapters.py). The modified `else` branch corresponds to a mixed wiring (engine-based reasoning adapter + a plain text-based tool parser such as Hermes), which the test mirrors with a fake engine-style reasoning parser plus the real Hermes2ProToolParser and the real Qwen3 tokenizer driving the real parse_delta streaming API.
